summary: Ambiguous invoice reference caused payment to be applied to wrong PO; request reversal and reallocation
description:
Issue summary: A single payment from vendor BrightArc (vendor_id: V-9982) was applied to PO-7789. The vendor submitted two partial invoices that shared the same vendor_reference token (BR-INV-2026-03). One invoice belonged to PO-7789 and the other to PO-7810. The payment engine matched the vendor_reference and auto-applied the whole payment to PO-7789, leaving PO-7810 unpaid and creating a $24,600 GL misallocation in account 2201.

Impact: Financial misstatement for March close if not corrected; downstream payment failure to PO-7810 blocking goods receipt and potential vendor escalation. Affects month-to-date AP aging and reserve calculations. No customer-facing outage but material for finance (>$20k).

Environment: Production finance dataset, BrightArc vendor profile, payments settled via payment-processor StripeConnect integration on 2026-03-02 14:12 UTC.

Steps to reproduce (how support triaged):
1) Reviewed BrightArc AP ledger and vendor invoices.
2) Searched for vendor_reference BR-INV-2026-03 and found two invoice records with different invoice_ids (INV-22011 and INV-22012) tied to different POs (PO-7789 & PO-7810).
3) Queried payment application logs: payment PAY-70321 matched on vendor_reference and applied to INV-22011/PO-7789 only.
4) Confirmed PO-7810 remains open and goods receipt was processed on 2026-03-01.

Logs & attachments: payment-apply.log excerpts (attached in ticket), screenshot of AP ledger showing duplicate vendor_reference, CSV export of invoices for vendor V-9982.

Initial findings & hypothesis: The auto-apply heuristic prioritizes exact vendor_reference and then earliest invoice date; because INV-22011 had an earlier invoice_date, the full payment was applied there. System did not detect duplicate vendor_reference across open POs. No evidence of duplicate payment from vendor. The payments-processor returned a single settlement.

Immediate risk mitigation performed: Placed a temporary hold on any further auto-applies for BrightArc by toggling vendor.auto_apply=false for vendor_id V-9982 (temporary config change recorded in change log). Accounting team alerted and advised to hold close-entry of affected GL account until reversal is processed.

Requested action: Finance ops needs a manual reversal of payment PAY-70321 from PO-7789/INV-22011 and re-apply $24,600 to PO-7810/INV-22012. After reallocation, request a short reconciliation report and journal entry guidance for GL 2201 adjustment.

Next steps owner & ETA: Assigned to Sophie Ramirez (Finance Helpdesk) to coordinate reversal with Payments team and AP system owners. Target to complete reversal and re-apply by 2026-03-10 to meet period-close timelines.

2026-03-03 14:30 - Payments Team (Amit Patel): Confirmed settlement completed via StripeConnect. We can perform an accounting reversal and create an internal application record to move allocation; cannot recollect funds from vendor at processor level.

2026-03-04 08:17 - Sophie Ramirez: Performed dry-run in staging AP system to validate re-apply flow; flow requires creating a reversing credit memo on INV-22011 then applying original payment to INV-22012. Staging notes attached.

2026-03-05 10:02 - GL Team (Maria Chen): Provided journal entry guidance for GL 2201: debit account 2201 $24,600 and credit clearing account 1205 $24,600, and then re-post after allocation. Please confirm once reversal is posted for final entries.
2026-03-08 16:48 - Sophie Ramirez: Reversal draft created in AP with reversing memo RM-881; waiting for finance approval to post. Scheduled posting for 2026-03-09 09:00 UTC pending approvals.

2026-03-09 12:05 - Sophie Ramirez: Reversal posted and payment re-applied. Invoice INV-22012 now marked paid. Attached reconciliation CSV and journal post reference JE-2026-03-78. Closing tasks: notify vendor and update vendor profile to require unique vendor_reference per PO to avoid recurrence.
resolution_notes: Manual reversal created (RM-881) and posted 2026-03-09. Payment PAY-70321 re-applied to INV-22012/PO-7810. Journal entry JE-2026-03-78 created to correct GL 2201. Vendor profile updated to require unique vendor_reference per PO; follow-up task created to add duplicate-reference detection in payments service.
follow_up_tasks: Create a ticket for engineering to add duplicate vendor_reference detection to payments auto-apply (owner: payments-team)
Update vendor onboarding docs to mandate unique invoice references for multi-PO billing (owner: vendor-ops)
